# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.

### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`

The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.

`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`

```yaml
# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
validate:
  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
  next: load
load:
  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
  next: apply
apply:
  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
```

```java
// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
public class ValidateOwner {
  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
  }
}
public class LoadOwner {
  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
    ownerOut.set(owner);
  }
}
public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
  }
}
public class SaveOwner {
  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
    repository.save(owner);
  }
}
public class RespondWithOwner {
  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
  }
}
```

`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`

```yaml
handle:
  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
```

```java
public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
  }
}
```

### Step wiring

Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
`method:`.

- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
  as `@Parameter T`.
- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
  branch; not calling it short-circuits.

### Function parameters

Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:

- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.

### Naming

Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).

Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
responder. Steps in between work with entities.

### Request body and validation

- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
  first step publishes it as a variable.
- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
  invalid body can return 400.

### Transactions

`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.

### Errors

Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.

### Security

Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:

```yaml
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
```

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:

  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.

### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`

The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.

`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`

```yaml
# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
validate:
  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
  next: load
load:
  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
  next: apply
apply:
  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
```

```java
// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
public class ValidateOwner {
  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
  }
}
public class LoadOwner {
  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
    ownerOut.set(owner);
  }
}
public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
  }
}
public class SaveOwner {
  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
    repository.save(owner);
  }
}
public class RespondWithOwner {
  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
  }
}
```

`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`

```yaml
handle:
  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
```

```java
public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
  }
}
```

### Step wiring

Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
`method:`.

- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
  as `@Parameter T`.
- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
  branch; not calling it short-circuits.

### Function parameters

Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:

- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.

### Naming

Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).

Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
responder. Steps in between work with entities.

### Request body and validation

- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
  first step publishes it as a variable.
- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
  invalid body can return 400.

### Transactions

`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.

### Errors

Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.

### Security

Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:

```yaml
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
```

1	package net.officefloor.hq.app.person;
2	
3	import java.util.List;
4	
5	/**
6	 * A person as the screen shows them; the last statement's due-total and date are null before the first, and
7	 * {@code retiredFrom} is null while they are not retired; {@code held} is whether they have any hold, {@code holds}
8	 * each hold, oldest first. {@code grade} is the grade in force on the sheet's today; {@code grades} every grade
9	 * recorded, each from its from-date. {@code terms} are the person's own terms in days in force on the sheet's today,
10	 * null when they have none then;
11	 * {@code contact} their contact, null when they have none. {@code clashing} is whether another sheet of the sheet's
12	 * tree uses their name or any of their aliases as a name or alias. {@code origin} is the sheet they were transferred
13	 * from, null when they were not transferred here. {@code pastRetirements} are the retirements they were unretired
14	 * from, oldest first. {@code tags} their tags, sorted (none: empty). {@code statements} each statement still standing as
15	 * {@code <statement date> <due-total>}, oldest first. {@code flag} is the reason of their flag while it is in force on
16	 * the sheet's today, "" otherwise. {@code approver} is the user who may approve their PENDING claims, "" when none.
17	 */
18	public record PersonResponse(long id, String name, String grade, int version, int statementCount, String statedTotal,
19	        String statementDate, boolean retired, String retiredFrom, boolean held,
20	        List<Grade> grades, List<HoldDates> holds, Integer terms, String contact,
21	        boolean clashing, String origin, List<RetirementDates> pastRetirements, List<String> tags,
22	        List<String> statements, String flag, String approver) {
23	
24	
25	    /** A grade recorded for the person, from its from-date (yyyy-mm-dd; null: from the beginning of time). */
26	    public record Grade(String grade, String from) {
27	    }
28	
29	    /** A hold on the person, from its from-date to its to-date, both inclusive (yyyy-mm-dd; null: open-ended). */
30	    public record HoldDates(String from, String to) {
31	    }
32	
33	    /** A retirement the person was unretired from, from its from-date to the day they were unretired (yyyy-mm-dd). */
34	    public record RetirementDates(String from, String to) {
35	    }
36	
37	    public static PersonResponse from(Person person, boolean clashing, String origin, String tags,
38	            List<String> statements, String flag, String approver) {
39	        return new PersonResponse(person.id(), person.name(), person.grade(), person.version(), person.statementCount(),
40	                person.statedTotal(), person.statementDate() == null ? null : person.statementDate().toString(),
41	                person.retired(), person.retiredFrom() == null ? null : person.retiredFrom().toString(),
42	                person.held(), person.grades().stream()
43	                        .map((g) -> new Grade(g.grade(), g.from() == null ? null : g.from().toString())).toList(),
44	                person.holds().stream().map((h) -> new HoldDates(h.from() == null ? null : h.from().toString(),
45	                        h.to() == null ? null : h.to().toString())).toList(), person.terms(),
46	                person.contact(), clashing, origin, person.pastRetirements().stream()
47	                        .map((r) -> new RetirementDates(r.from().toString(), r.to().toString())).toList(),
48	                tags == null ? List.of() : List.of(tags.split(",")), statements,
49	                flag == null ? "" : flag, approver == null ? "" : approver);
50	    }
51	}

# OfficeFloor REST wiring

Domain REST endpoints are declared here as OfficeFloor YAML, served by the
`officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` inside the Spring Boot host. Put them under `rest/api/` so
their paths start with `/api/` — `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend; a non-`/api/`
path returns the SPA's `index.html` instead of your endpoint. Directory nesting maps to path
segments, so `rest/api/owners.GET.yml` → `GET /api/owners`. Each route is its own file:

```
# officefloor/rest/api/<path>.GET.yml   (or .POST.yml, {param}.GET.yml, ...)
service:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.<SomeLogic>   # a class with a service(...) method
```

The logic class's `service(...)` method takes injected dependencies (Spring `@Service` beans, the
data layer) and a `net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse<T>` to send the response.

a543e0ba6a1c8f7e8 completed Agent "Server totals and settings logic" completed ## Server-side totals, rates & settings — findings ### 1. Per-person totals (claimed, due, stated total) **There is no server-side "claimed"/"due" total per person.** `PersonResponse` (person/PersonResponse.java:20-24) carries only `statementCount`, `statedTotal`, `statementDate`, `statements`; no claimed/due sum. `RespondWithPeople` just maps `Person` → `PersonResponse`. Totals shown on the sheet are summed in the front end (outside my scope) from per-claim figures. **Per-claim `due` is not sent live.** `ClaimResponse.due` is only the *fixed* settle-time due (`claim.due()`, ClaimResponse.java:44), plus `statedDue`. The live due (`Claim.due(rate, floor, late, rounding)`) is computed server-side only in: - `ClaimDueNow.of` (claim/ClaimDueNow.java:24-33) — used by settle/approve/review checks and the status log. - `statement/TakeStatement` and `rollup/RollupService`. **Statement due-total** — statement/TakeStatement.java (~lines 40-95): ```java for (Claim c : claims) { if (!person.counts(c, today)) continue; // deferred / retired-open excluded if (c.deferred(today)) { unbind; continue; } BigDecimal d = c.due(rate, dated.floorOn(c.date()), dated.lateCharge(today, person), rounding); ... bind c (stated=true, statedDue=d) total = total == null ? d : total.add(d); // n/a rate → total stays null for that claim } person.statedTotal = total == null ? "n/a" : total.setScale(2) ``` - Includes OPEN, PENDING, SETTLED (via `Claim.counts(held)`); excludes DRAFT/VOID/DELETED/REVIEW and deferred. - `Person.counts` (Person.java:166) — `heldOn` is now just `retiredOn(today)` (Person.java:182-184), so **holds do not exclude claims**, despite `Person` javadoc (line 15-16: "their open claims dated within one … count in no live total") and `Claim` javadoc ("a held OPEN or PENDING claim leaves the live totals as a hold on its person would") — both contradicted by code. `Claim.held` is never read in any totals path. - A settled claim contributes its fixed `due`; a bound claim its `statedDue`. **Rollup** (rollup/RollupService.java ~30-110): sums per-person due over children sheets in the tree (`Descendants`), using the same `Claim.due(...)` with each sheet's own rates/floor/late/rounding, `person.counts(c, today)`; result "n/a" if any counting claim has no rate. Recorded as `ROLLUP` audit line and snapshotted (`SnapshotRollup`). **Pools** (pool/PoolRepository.java ~100-140): a pool's lead gets `lead` share, others `share`; `m.held()` (person has any hold) is passed through — the pool cut is where a hold actually bites (Person.java:179-181 says "it only takes away their pool cut"). **AsOf** (asof/*): `RecordSheetDay` snapshots each sheet day; `AsOfView`/`AsOfReader` re-read the stored state as of a past day (read-only views; same calculation). ### 2. Rates — rate/Rate.java, RateRepository - `Rate.inForce(rates, grade, claim)` (Rate.java ~25-50): of the grade's rates whose `from` ≤ claim.date **and** `appliesTo(claim)`, take the latest `from` (ties: latest `saved`). `null` → n/a. - `appliesTo(claim)`: `!forwardOnly || claim.added() > saved` — forward-only rates only reach claims *added* after the rate was saved (sequence shared with `claim.added`). - Grade used is `person.gradeOn(claim.date())` (grade in force on the claim's date, not today). - A rate change re-figures every live (unsettled, unbound) claim; settled `due` and bound `statedDue` are frozen. ### 3. Settings — setting/DatedSettings.java, SettingRepository.java Every setting is stored with a from-date (`SettingRepository.save*` with `from`, default sheet today); `DatedSettings` holds lists and picks **the one with the latest from-date on or before the date asked**: | Setting | Read as of | Effect | |---|---|---| | `floorOn(date)` | claim date | minimum due (not for corrections) | | `capOn` | claim date | **CAP is loaded and saved/audited but never applied in `Claim.due`** — dead in figures | | `latePctOn(boundary)` | each 30-day boundary | compounding late charge | | `graceDays` / `GradeGrace` | claim date, by person grade then sheet | added to due-by before late | | `termsFor(grade,date)` / `GradeTerms` | sheet today at creation (via `NewDueBy`) | business days to due-by | | `rounding(sheet, today, claims)` | claim date (correction: corrected claim's date) | `RoundingSetting` mode in force, else `PolicyDate` split HALF_UP / HALF_EVEN | | `ClerkLimit` / `GradeClerkLimit` | sheet today | clerk settle above → PENDING | | `ReviewThreshold` | sheet today | open above → REVIEW | | `NoteThreshold` | sheet today | claim amount above requires a note | | `ProofThreshold` / `GradeProofThreshold` / `ProofKinds` | sheet today | settle needs N proofs (of kinds) | | `AlertThreshold`, `EscalateAfter`, `ReviewSla` | sheet today | flagging overdue/escalation figures | | `Pot` | sheet today | pool pot | | `EntryDate` | — | earliest claim date accepted | | `FiscalStartMonth`, `PeriodNumberingFrom` | — | period generation & per-period numbering | | `DefaultGrade` | today | grade given to new people with none | | `Delegation` | dates | a steward's powers delegated to a clerk for a window | | `Permissions` / `Role` / `UserRole` | — | per-user role STEWARD / CLERK / VIEWER; Fixes `due = ClaimDueNow` (floor + late charge frozen). If user is CLERK (and not delegated) and due > clerk limit (grade clerk limit for the person's grade, else sheet's) → PENDING instead (due not fixed? — it **is** fixed: `withStatus(PENDING, number, due, …)`, ApplyClaimAction ~L120). - **APPROVE/REJECT** (PENDING→SETTLED / →OPEN): steward or the person's `approver` only; REJECT clears `due` (`asOpenUnbound`). - **VOID**: DRAFT/OPEN/PENDING/REVIEW always; SETTLED only by STEWARD within 7 days (`settledOn.plusDays(7)` vs today; date from status log). - **DELETE/RESTORE**: DRAFT only; restore only on the sheet-today it was deleted. - **REVIEW**: steward only, REVIEW→OPEN. - Edit only DRAFT (`CheckClaimDraft`); `CheckClaimLinesAmount` requires lines total = amount when lines exist; `NoteThreshold` requires a note above it. - **Split** (`SplitClaim`): OPEN only, amount strictly between 0 and claim amount, new claim numbered next and `splitFrom`; the kept one loses its stated figure (`splitKeeping`). - **Defer** (`CheckClaimDeferral`): OPEN only, date after today. **Waive** (`CheckClaimWaive`): steward only, overdue only. **Remind**: overdue, once per day. **Redate**: DRAFT or OPEN, period open on both dates, renumber under period numbering, keeps due-by. **Reassign**: to a non-retired person, not settled. **Proof**: `takesProof`; kind must be in `ProofKinds`. - **Corrections** (`CheckClaimInputCorrects`): negative amount; must name a SETTLED claim of the same person; |amount| ≤ its due. - **Bulk settle** (`CheckBulkSettle`, `SaveClaimBatch`): settles each eligible OPEN claim, gives a batch number; skips (not refuses) ineligible ones. ### Periods — period/* States: open → soft-closed → closed, plus locked. `CheckClaimPeriodOpen` / `CheckClaimInputPeriodOpen`: a claim dated in a **closed** or **locked** period cannot be added/edited/settled/voided/redated. **Soft-closed**: allowed, but `MarkLateEntry` flags the claim `lateEntry` (shown in ClaimResponse). `AutoClosePeriods` closes periods whose end + N days passed on loading. Reopen: steward only. Periods must not overlap (`CheckPeriodFits`). ### People — person/* - **Hold** (`HoldPerson`, from/to inclusive): blocks settling claims dated within (CheckClaimHold) and removes pool cut; does not change totals (code). - **Flag** (`CheckFlagSteward`): steward only; reason shown while in force on today. - **Retire**: from a date; claims dated after it refused (`retiredBefore`); once reached, open claims drop from due totals and claimed. Unretire records a past retirement whose window still refuses claims. - **Transfer/Move/Merge**: transfer copies the person to another sheet of the tree (refused if name clashes, `CheckTransfer`); undo within the same day (`CheckTransferUndo`); merge (`CheckMerge`) moves claims to the target, refused if either is retired or has PENDING claims. - **Name unique** (`CheckPersonNameUnique`, case-insensitive) and `StalePersonException` on version mismatch. ### Imports - **importpeople**: lines `name[,grade]`; skips existing names (counted as not added), grade defaults to `DefaultGrade`. - **opening** (import openings): creates SETTLED claims with given due, dated given date; refused per line if period closed. - **paste**: claims pasted as DRAFTs (`SavePastedClaims`), dueBy computed per row. - **quickadd**: a single-line form → DRAFT claim. ### Statements — statement/* `TakeStatement` binds every counting non-deferred claim to its due now (`stated=true, statedDue`), records the total; `CancelStatement` unbinds the claims bound by the last statement and restores the previous one's total. `StatementAsOf` takes a statement as at a past date. ### Pipeline inconsistencies (YAML) - `claims/{claimId}/settle/*` and the bulk settle pipeline: bulk path does **not** run `CheckClaimNotLocked`. - `paste` and `quickadd` don't run `CheckClaimInputNotRetired`. - `opening` import skips `CheckNotViewer`. 1	package net.officefloor.hq.app.claim;
     2	
     3	/**
     4	 * Where a claim is in its life: it starts DRAFT, is opened and then settled; a clerk settling one whose due is above
     5	 * the clerk limit makes it PENDING instead, until a steward approves it (SETTLED) or rejects it (OPEN again). A DRAFT,
     6	 * OPEN or PENDING claim can be voided, and a steward may void a SETTLED one within 7 days of its settlement. Only a
     7	 * DRAFT can be edited. VOID is final. A DRAFT can be deleted (DELETED), and restored to a DRAFT on the sheet's today it
     8	 * was deleted; a DELETED claim counts nowhere. Only OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED claims count toward the totals. A claim
     9	 * whose due is above the sheet's review threshold goes to REVIEW when opened instead of OPEN, until a steward reviews it
    10	 * (OPEN); a REVIEW claim counts in no total, cannot be edited, settled or split, and can be voided.
    11	 */
    12	public enum ClaimStatus {

    14	
    15	    /** Whether a claim with this status is open: OPEN, or PENDING (handled like an open claim). */
    16	    public boolean open() {
    17	        return this == OPEN || this == PENDING;
    18	    }
    19	}

1	package net.officefloor.hq.app.rollup;
     2	
     3	import java.math.BigDecimal;
     4	import java.time.LocalDate;
     5	import java.util.ArrayList;
     6	import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
     7	import java.util.List;
     8	import java.util.Map;
     9	import net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.Claim;
    10	import net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.ClaimRepository;
    11	import net.officefloor.hq.app.claim.Rounding;
    12	import net.officefloor.hq.app.person.Person;
    13	import net.officefloor.hq.app.person.PersonRepository;
    14	import net.officefloor.hq.app.rate.Rate;
    15	import net.officefloor.hq.app.rate.RateRepository;
    16	import net.officefloor.hq.app.setting.Cap;
    17	import net.officefloor.hq.app.setting.DatedSettings;
    18	import net.officefloor.hq.app.setting.SettingRepository;
    19	import net.officefloor.hq.app.sheet.SheetRepository;
    20	import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
    21	
    22	/**
    23	 * Works out a sheet's figures as the screen shows them: a person's claimed is their counting claims' amounts
    24	 * added up (a held claim's too, in every figure: a hold only takes away a pool cut; none once their retirement date is reached), leaving out corrections; their due-total those claims' dues (live figures rounded by its policy date, plus
    25	 * any late charge, at the late percent in force on each 30-day boundary, on the overdue ones, then raised to the floor in force on each claim's date) added up, at most the cap in force on the sheet's today; n/a when their grade on the sheet's today has no
    26	 * rate there and no counting claim has a figure (kept, or at the rate for the grade in force on its date). Their overdue-total
    27	 * is the dues of their overdue counting claims added up (skipping n/a, not capped). The sheet's totals add these up, skipping n/a;
    28	 * its due-total and overdue-total leave out the single highest and lowest person's figure when three or more have one.
    29	 */
    30	@Service
    31	public class RollupService {
    32	
    33	    private static final String NA = "n/a";
    34	
    35	    private final PersonRepository people;
    36	    private final ClaimRepository claims;
    37	    private final RateRepository rates;
    38	    private final SheetRepository sheets;
    39	    private final SettingRepository settings;
    40	
    41	    public RollupService(PersonRepository people, ClaimRepository claims, RateRepository rates,
    42	            SheetRepository sheets, SettingRepository settings) {
    43	        this.people = people;
    44	        this.claims = claims;
    45	        this.rates = rates;
    46	        this.sheets = sheets;
    47	        this.settings = settings;
    48	    }
    49	
    50	    /** The sheet's figures as the store holds them now. */
    51	    public Rollup compute(String sheetId) {
    52	        LocalDate today = sheets.today(sheetId);
    53	        List<Rate> sheetRates = rates.findAll(sheetId);
    54	        DatedSettings dated = settings.dated(sheetId);
    55	        BigDecimal cap = dated.capOn(today);
    56	        List<Claim> sheetClaims = claims.findAll(sheetId);
    57	        Rounding rounding = settings.rounding(sheetId, today, sheetClaims);
    58	        Map<Long, Rollup.Figures> figures = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    59	        BigDecimal claimedTotal = BigDecimal.ZERO.setScale(2);
    60	        List<BigDecimal> dues = new ArrayList<>();
    61	        List<BigDecimal> overdues = new ArrayList<>();
    62	        for (Person person : people.findAll(sheetId)) {
    63	            BigDecimal claimed = BigDecimal.ZERO.setScale(2);
    64	            BigDecimal due = BigDecimal.ZERO.setScale(2);
    65	            BigDecimal overdue = BigDecimal.ZERO.setScale(2);
    66	            boolean kept = false;
    67	            for (Claim claim : sheetClaims) {
    68	                if (claim.personId() != person.id()) {
    69	                    continue;
    70	                }
    71	                if (!claim.correction() && person.countsClaimed(claim, today)) {
    72	                    claimed = claimed.add(claim.amount());
    73	                }
    74	                if (!person.counts(claim, today)) {
    75	                    continue;
    76	                }
    77	                kept |= claim.keepsFigure();
    78	                BigDecimal figure = claim.due(Rate.inForce(sheetRates, person.gradeOn(claim.date()), claim),
    79	                        dated.floorOn(claim.date()), dated.lateCharge(today, person), rounding);
    80	                if (figure != null) {
    81	                    kept = true;
    82	                    due = due.add(figure);
    83	                    if (claim.overdue(today, dated.graceFor(person, claim))) {
    84	                        overdue = overdue.add(figure);
    85	                    }
    86	                }
    87	            }
    88	            boolean na = Rate.inForce(sheetRates, person.grade(), today) == null && !kept;
    89	            due = Cap.apply(cap, due);
    90	            claimedTotal = claimedTotal.add(claimed);
    91	            if (!na) {
    92	                dues.add(due);
    93	            }
    94	            overdues.add(overdue);
    95	            figures.put(person.id(), new Rollup.Figures(person.name(), show(claimed), na ? NA : show(due), show(overdue)));
    96	        }
    97	        return new Rollup(figures, show(claimedTotal), show(trimmedTotal(dues)), show(trimmedTotal(overdues)),
    98	                settings.alertThreshold(sheetId));
    99	    }
   100	
   101	    /** The figures added up, leaving out the single highest and single lowest when there are three or more. */
   102	    private static BigDecimal trimmedTotal(List<BigDecimal> values) {
   103	        List<BigDecimal> sorted = new ArrayList<>(values);
   104	        sorted.sort(null);
   105	        if (sorted.size() >= 3) {
   106	            sorted = sorted.subList(1, sorted.size() - 1);
   107	        }
   108	        return sorted.stream().reduce(BigDecimal.ZERO.setScale(2), BigDecimal::add);
   109	    }
   110	
   111	    private static String show(BigDecimal value) {
   112	        return value.setScale(2).toPlainString();
   113	    }
   114	}

Per-person figures are **computed client-side** in `features/people/totals.ts` and `features/claims/figures.ts`; the server only sends raw claims, rates, settings. ### features/claims/figures.ts - `liveDue(claim, ctx)` (L12-58): re-implements `Claim.due` in TS — `due ?? (stated ? statedDue : amount*rate/100)`, floor via `floorOn(claim.date)`, late charge via `lateCharge(claim, today)` with 30-day boundaries and compounding. Rounding: `roundHalfUp` before policy date, `roundHalfEven` on/after (L40-48), **but ignores the dated `rounding` mode setting** (server `Rounding.modeFor` checks `modes.apply(date)` first) and **ignores the correction rule** (server rounds a correction by the corrected claim's date). - Grace: uses `settings.graceDays` (sheet-level, an auto-close setting!) instead of the grade's grace in force on the claim's date (L33) — mismatch with `DatedSettings.graceFor`. - `overdue(claim, today)` (L60-66): `open && !deferred && dueBy < today` — no grace. - Waived claims: honoured (L36). ### features/people/totals.ts - `claimed(person, claims, today)` (L8-20): sums `amount` of claims with status OPEN/PENDING/SETTLED, not deferred, **and not `claim.held`** (L14) — server `Person.countsClaimed` says a hold does not take a claim out of claimed, and excludes all claims once retired; TS excludes retired only for OPEN. - `dueTotal(person, claims, ctx)` (L22-45): sums `liveDue` of counting claims; `n/a` if any counting claim has null due; then caps by `settings.cap` (today's cap). Excludes `claim.held` claims (L30) unless stated — matches the Claim javadoc, not Person.counts. - testids: `person-claimed`, `person-due`, `person-overdue-count`, `person-stated-total`. ### Permissions in UI (features/session/role.ts) - Hides settle/void/approve buttons by `role` from settings; doesn't consider delegations (L20) — server's `roleOf` does. ### Other - `features/aging/buckets.ts`: 0-30/31-60/61-90/90+ by `today - dueBy` for overdue claims. - `features/overdue`: count of `overdue()` claims per person. - `features/pools/cut.ts`: shares pot by members, lead gets remainder; a held person gets 0. Main duplication: due logic exists in Java (`Claim.due`, `LateCharge`, `Rounding`) and again in TS (`figures.ts`, `totals.ts`), with diverging rules for holds, grace, rounding mode, corrections, retirement. total_tokens: 18033 tokens
